title: 127 Evaluation of sire selection and maternal influence on feed efficiency in Katahdin sheep
content:
Abstract
Genetic selection focused on feed efficiency may be valuable in lowering lamb feed costs for growth and maintenance requirements without compromising growth. The Vytelle Sense system allows measurement of individual lamb DMI to identify feed efficient lambs. The aim of this study was to evaluate the impact of sire selection and maternal influence on lamb residual feed intake (RFI), gain:feed (G:F), average daily gain (ADG), and daily DMI. Sires (n = 22) bred to Katahdin ewes at the Virginia Tech Southwest Virginia Agricultural Research and Extension Center (SWAREC), North Carolina State University (NCSU), and West Virginia University (WVU) were utilized to evaluate sire impact on progeny feed efficiency. Post-weaning, progeny were evaluated on a Vytelle Sense system between 2019 and 2024. RFI was calculated as the difference between actual and expected DMI (DMI predicted based on ADG and metabolic body size). Statistical analyses were performed using PROC Mixed SAS (SAS Institute, Cary, NC). Individual sire had a significant effect on growing lamb RFI, G:F, ADG, and daily DMI (P < 0.05). To evaluate sire impact on RFI across multiple locations, sires (n = 7) that were bred to ewes at two or more locations were analyzed separately. Genetic connectedness between locations allowed for comparisons of progeny performance. Estimates of sire mean RFI did not differ across locations (P > 0.10). However, significance was detected between locations for G:F, ADG, and daily DMI (P < 0.05). To identify if maternal selection impacts feed efficiency, ewe families (n = 17) from across the three universities were established by identifying a foundation ewe within each maternal line. Genetic connectedness between locations allowed for comparisons of progeny performance. Ewe family did not impact progeny RFI (P > 0.10). However, significance was detected between ewe families for G:F, ADG, and daily DMI (P < 0.05). Variation between sires indicates potential sire impact on progeny feed efficiency. Further studies are required to evaluate the consistency of sire RFI trends across multiple locations and maternal impact on feed efficiency.
